extracted.intended_audience: early-career researchers applying for the DFG Emmy Noether Programme (independent junior research group funding) in Germany
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting an application for the DFG Emmy Noether Programme to obtain funding to lead an independent junior research group in Germany. Covers eligibility, selection expectations, host-institution commitments, and desired candidate profile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must show a strong track record and impressive academic and scientific records that promise outstanding careers in science or the humanities; scientific excellence is a key criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The brochure repeatedly emphasises that Emmy Noether fellows have passed a rigorous selection process and are 'among the best.' More than 70 fellows have been offered professorships, and the programme seeks the best researchers regardless of current location. Scientific excellence is considered alongside independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrated independent research after doctorate
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must demonstrate that they have conducted independent research after obtaining their doctorates and are able to build independent academic careers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text states explicitly: 'applicants must demonstrate that they have conducted independent research after obtaining their doctorates' and that they 'need to have cut themselves loose from their professors.' Independence in research activity is required as evidence the candidate can lead an independent group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence and mobility (geographic and thematic)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'They need to have cut themselves loose from their professors, meaning they should be independent and mobile, both geographically and thematically.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independence includes thematic autonomy (own research profile) and willingness/ability to move geographically. The programme targets candidates who are independent of prior supervisors and can lead their own research direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: International experience or networking
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates should have worked abroad for at least one year, or, if not, be well networked internationally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The brochure: 'Candidates should have worked abroad for at least one year. It is irrelevant whether this international research experience was part of their doctoral training or gained afterwards... Applicants who have not done any research outside Germany, but who are well networked internationally, also have a good chance of being accepted.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Letter of commitment from a hiring institution / host conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Each application must include a letter of commitment from a hiring institution that is willing to employ the candidate and provide the necessary working conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The letter must confirm employment and necessary working conditions (space, infrastructure, rights). The brochure highlights the importance of institutional support and warns that lack of space, integration or teaching/supervision rights at some universities can impede successful group operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility window after doctorate
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates may be admitted into the programme up to four years after they have finished their doctorates (new rule replacing previously narrow age restrictions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This timing rule defines the eligible cohort. The brochure notes the change from earlier narrow age limits to allow admission within four years post-PhD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process: written proposal and in-person presentation to expert committees
rubrics_metrics.description: Junior research group leaders are generally handpicked by expert committees on the basis of written proposals and in-person presentations of their research projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is rigorous and peer-review based. Successful applicants may be funded for five years (six in exceptional cases). The DFG's review and expert-committee procedures constitute a 'DFG seal of approval.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to recruit and lead a team (leadership and management skills)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should be prepared to head an independent junior research group: recruit and supervise doctoral students, motivate and direct a team, manage budgets, and undertake administrative/management tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The brochure describes responsibilities: supervising doctoral students, writing proposals to obtain additional funds, staffing and lab space needs, and balancing teaching/administration. Leadership experience and potential are highlighted as important for future career development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and quality of project concept, schedule and finances
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications (and host institutions/universities) should show transparent planning: clear rules on schedule, finances, concept, supervision and support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: University experts stress the importance of transparency and clear rules so young researchers know planning requirements for schedule, finances and concept, and how they will be supervised and supported. Proposal culture forces applicants to articulate research plans clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit to German academic qualification path / potential to qualify as university lecturer
rubrics_metrics.description: The programme seeks candidates who wish to qualify in Germany as university lecturers and whose profile indicates a trajectory toward professorship (fast-track potential).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text frames the ENP as a 'turbo programme' to accelerate the qualification phase leading to professorship within five to six years. Track record and resource usage that improve chances of chair appointments (publications, third-party fundraising) are valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary suitability and flexibility in funding format
rubrics_metrics.description: The ENP is open to all disciplines but has traditionally funded more natural and life sciences; humanities and social scientists are eligible and may be funded as project leaders even without forming a junior research group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The brochure notes the overwhelming majority of fellows are in natural/life sciences but the ENP seeks to support humanities as they adopt team research models; funding formats may adapt (e.g., project leader funding) to disciplinary norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host-institution integration and long-term prospects
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation considers how well the host university integrates the fellow (teaching rights, supervision rights, lab/office space) and whether there are prospects for longer-term career paths (tenure-track or professorship).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The brochure discusses common challenges: lack of space, insufficient integration (e.g., not being permitted to teach or fully supervise doctoral students), and universities being called upon to offer long-term perspectives and contribute funding from the beginning for tenure-track possibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willingness/ability to raise additional third-party funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Successful junior research group leaders often complement DFG funding by raising third-party funds and demonstrating capacity in fundraising.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements from fellows and university experts highlight that experience with third-party fundraising and publishing are 'key criteria for success' when negotiating chair appointments and for growing a group (staff, equipment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation and communication skills (for visibility and networking)
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates should be able to present their research convincingly in-person and engage with networks, media and political/scientific stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The brochure mentions in-person presentations being part of the selection process, the value of annual meetings and forums for feedback, and fellows' engagement with media and policymakers as beneficial for profile and career advancement.
